gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the rapid-trigger figure on these under-$50 boards is each maker's adjustment step, not a measured value, and that put on one basis it runs from 0.1 mm (Redragon K617 HE) through 0.04 mm (Aula WIN60 HE / WIN68 HE standard; 0.02 mm is the Max version only) to 0.01 mm (MCHOSE Ace 60 Pro, Epomaker HE68 Lite, Gamakay NS68).
standout_why: Compared against hlplanet.com (cited), mechanicalkeyboard.net's HE68 Lite review (cited), chronicreload.com and deal.ai. hlplanet gives no rapid-trigger, scan-rate or wireless-polling figure for any board under $60. mechanicalkeyboard.net covers only the HE68 Lite (0.01 mm steps, 128 kHz scan, and that 0.125 ms is the polling interval) and names none of the other candidates. chronicreload has part of it: 0.02 mm for the WIN60 HE and WIN68 HE and 0.1 mm for the K617 HE, but it mixes 'step distance' and 'accuracy' undefined and never splits Aula standard from Max. deal.ai gives no rapid-trigger figure in mm. The table and the Aula 0.04 mm standard figure are new; the score would be 1 on the latency point alone. PC Gamer's cited list and its NS68 review both came back truncated to navigation, so I could not compare against them.
decides: It confirms the top tier and demotes the Aula. On the makers' own figures the Gamakay NS68 wired ($36.79, linkable through our Gamakay program) matches the MCHOSE Ace 60 Pro ($37.40) and Epomaker HE68 Lite ($42.49) at 0.01 mm with 8,000 Hz polling, so it belongs in the table as a near-tie we can link, and it is a 65% board with arrow keys. ChatGPT's answer credited the standard Aula WIN60 HE with 0.02 mm; the Aula Gear store says the standard is 0.04 mm and only the Max is 0.02 mm. The Redragon K617 HE is coarsest at 0.1 mm, and Redragon itself warns the 0.1-0.2 mm setting may be affected by component tolerances. The NS68 tri-mode ($39.99) should not be described as 8K wireless until Gamakay's page is read.
candidates: Gamakay x NaughShark NS68 (wired and tri-mode)
